nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, Moore's minimal automaton of $M$ has exactly as many states as there are Nerode classes of the language accepted by $M$.
nodes.title: Moore's automaton has one state per Nerode class

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, two states $p$ and $q$ of $M$ are related by Moore's relation if and only if they have the same continuation language: for every word $w$, $M$ started at $p$ accepts $w$ exactly when $M$ started at $q$ accepts $w$.
nodes.title: Correctness of Moore's refinement

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states. For a reachable state $s$ of $M$, its Moore class is the equivalence class of $s$ among the reachable states of $M$ under Moore's relation; it is a state of Moore's minimal automaton of $M$.
nodes.title: Moore class of a reachable state

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, Moore's minimal automaton of $M$ accepts exactly the language accepted by $M$.
nodes.title: Moore's automaton accepts the same language

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, Moore's minimal automaton of $M$ has as states the classes of reachable states of $M$ under Moore's relation. Its start state is the class of the start state of $M$; reading a letter $a$ sends the class of a reachable state $s$ to the class of the state that $M$ reaches from $s$ on $a$; and the class of $s$ is accepting exactly when $s$ is an accepting…
nodes.title: Moore's minimal automaton

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states. The states of Moore's minimal automaton of $M$ are in bijection with the reachable residual languages of $M$: the bijection sends the class of a reachable state $s$ to the continuation language of $s$, the set of words that $M$ accepts when started at $s$.
nodes.title: Moore classes are the reachable residuals

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, and write $R$ for one round of Moore's refinement. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every set $E$ of pairs of states of $M$, there is $k \le n$ such that the stopping Moore iteration from $E$ with budget $n$ returns $R^k(E)$, and if $k < n$ then $R^k(E)$ is a fixed point of $R$, that is, $R(R^k(E)) = R^k(E)$.
nodes.title: Output of the stopping Moore iteration

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, and write $R$ for one round of Moore's refinement. For a set $E$ of pairs of states of $M$ and a budget $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the stopping Moore iteration is defined by recursion on $n$: with budget $0$ it returns $E$; with budget $n + 1$ it returns $E$ if $R(E) = E$, and otherwise the stopping Moore iteration from $R(E)$ with budget $n$.
nodes.title: Stopping Moore iteration

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ over a finite alphabet with finite set of states $Q$, Moore's relation is the set of pairs of states obtained from $Q \times Q$ by repeating rounds of Moore's refinement until a round changes nothing, for at most $|Q \times Q|$ rounds.
nodes.title: Moore's relation

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states. Each state of Moore's minimal automaton of $M$, a class of reachable states of $M$, is sent to the continuation language of any member $s$, the set of words that $M$ accepts when started at $s$; this is a reachable residual language of $M$. It does not depend on the choice of $s$, because Moore-related states have the same continuation language.
nodes.title: Continuation language of a Moore class

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$, two reachable states $p$ and $q$ of $M$ are related when the pair $(p, q)$ lies in Moore's relation of $M$; this relation is an equivalence relation on the reachable states of $M$.
nodes.title: Moore equivalence on reachable states

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$, these are the equivalence classes of the reachable states of $M$ under Moore equivalence, that is, under Moore's relation of $M$ restricted to reachable states. They are the states of Moore's minimal automaton.
nodes.title: States of Moore's automaton

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with state set $S$ and transition function $\delta$. One round of Moore's refinement sends a set $E \subseteq S \times S$ of pairs of states to the set of pairs $(p, q) \in S \times S$ such that $p$ is accepting if and only if $q$ is accepting and, for every letter $a$, the pair $(\delta(p, a), \delta(q, a))$ lies in $E$.
nodes.title: Moore refinement step

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA. Renaming each state of Moore's minimal automaton of $M$, a class of reachable states, to the continuation language accepted from its members turns Moore's automaton into exactly the minimized DFA of $M$, whose states are the reachable continuation languages of $M$.
nodes.title: Moore's automaton is the minimal automaton

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA. If a set $Z$ of pairs of states of $M$ is contained in its image under one round of Moore's refinement, then $Z$ is contained in Moore's relation of $M$.
nodes.title: Moore's relation contains every post-fixed point

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
